searchText: What would you change in that new contract except for the data type? We could reject 0x00 withdrawal credentials in it; but I am not sure how helpful will this be. I agree that new contracts are cleaner, my only preference would be to have them in a separate EIP that would also say that old deposit contract is about to be deprecated in the mid-term future (one or two forks after) > just updating gossip validation It implies introducing RLP into clients that doesn't support it which is also a big change for them. I would like to know which clients would be affected by this. If it's one or two then RLP might be less intrusive than the `payload_root` alright, seems <@&898338229407870986> is gonna be the one without `block_hash` check in gossip if we take this path? I will open a PR soon for that Edit: https://github.com/grandinetech/grandine/pull/1040 Ah this is a good idea. We thought early on committing to the whole envelope to avoid equivocations, but this was dismissed because of circular dependencies. The root of only the payload does work, but the builder can equivocate on the requests anyways right? The same applies to RLP blockhash anyway requests are checked against the bid and rejected if they don't match, i think `block_hash` is the only part of the commitment that isn't check on gossip yet Yes that's true That was the only reason we added the root, forgot that Here's a PR with the `payload_root` in the bid. https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5820 Yeah this looks nice. As long as we're good with breaking Sepolia, I support this. I made this PR to merge those other (non block hash) checks from 5770: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5821 I'll get that merged soon & rebase both payload uniqueness solutions.
